lessonTitle: The Simple Rankine Cycle: Boiler, Turbine, Condenser and Pump

blocks.text: A coal-fired power station produces 500 MW by boiling water at high pressure, expanding the steam through a turbine, condensing it at a pressure far below atmospheric and pumping the water back to the boiler. Four devices, four processes, one loop: the Rankine cycle.

blocks.markdown: The **ideal Rankine cycle** is the standard model of a steam power plant. The working fluid circulates through four steady-flow devices, and in the ideal cycle every device is internally reversible and there are no pressure drops in the pipes and heat exchangers.

items: 1-2: isentropic compression of saturated liquid in the **pump**, from condenser pressure to boiler pressure.
2-3: constant-pressure heat addition in the **boiler**: heating the compressed liquid, boiling it, and superheating it.
3-4: isentropic expansion in the **turbine**, producing work, to the condenser pressure, usually a wet mixture.
4-1: constant-pressure heat rejection in the **condenser**, ending as saturated liquid.

blocks.markdown: On a **T-s diagram** the saturation dome is a bell. State 1 sits on the saturated liquid line. The pump line 1-2 is almost vertical and very short. Process 2-3 rises up the liquid side of the dome, runs horizontally across the dome during boiling and continues rising in the superheated region. The turbine line 3-4 is a vertical drop, and the condenser line 4-1 runs horizontally at the saturation temperature of the condenser pressure back to the liquid line.

blocks.title: Rankine cycle energy terms
blocks.text: Per kilogram of steam: pump work $w_p=h_2-h_1\approx v_1(p_2-p_1)$; heat input $q_{in}=h_3-h_2$; turbine work $w_t=h_3-h_4$; heat rejected $q_{out}=h_4-h_1$. All terms are in kJ/kg and all devices are adiabatic except the heat exchangers.

blocks.caption: Thermal efficiency of the ideal Rankine cycle

blocks.title: Steam plant with boiler at 3 MPa and 400 C
blocks.prompt: Steam leaves the boiler at 3 MPa and 400 C (h3 = 3231.7 kJ/kg, s3 = 6.9235 kJ/(kg K), approximate table values). The condenser pressure is 10 kPa, where hf = 191.81 kJ/kg, vf = 0.001010 m$^3$/kg, hfg = 2392.1 kJ/kg, sf = 0.6492 and sfg = 7.4996 kJ/(kg K). Find the net work, heat input and efficiency.

steps.text: State 1 is saturated liquid at 10 kPa. Pump work for incompressible liquid.
State 4 from isentropic expansion: $s_4=s_3$, so find the quality.

blocks.answer: w_net = 1036 kJ/kg, q_in = 3037 kJ/kg and the efficiency is about 34.1 %. The pump uses only 0.3 % of the turbine work.

rows: Wetter exit; limited by cooling water temperature and air leakage
blocks.caption: Ways to improve the ideal Rankine cycle

blocks.markdown: The efficiency increases when the **average temperature at which heat is added** rises or when the **temperature at which heat is rejected** falls, the same reasoning that governs the Carnot efficiency $1-T_L/T_H$. A higher boiler pressure raises the boiling temperature; a lower condenser pressure lowers the saturation temperature in the condenser, since for a pure substance $T_{sat}$ depends only on pressure.

blocks.title: Rating a cycle from its enthalpies
blocks.prompt: A Rankine plant has h1 = 250, h2 = 256, h3 = 3300 and h4 = 2200 kJ/kg (values supplied for the exercise). Find the net work and efficiency.

blocks.title: Moisture limit
blocks.text: Wet steam droplets erode turbine blades. Designers keep the exit quality above about 0.85 to 0.90, which limits how far the boiler pressure can be raised without raising the peak temperature or adding reheat.

blocks.title: Pump work is small
blocks.text: Liquid is nearly incompressible, so the pump work is a tiny fraction of the turbine work. The back work ratio of a Rankine cycle is therefore tiny compared with that of a gas turbine.

points: The ideal Rankine cycle has isentropic pump, constant-pressure boiler, isentropic turbine and constant-pressure condenser.
Use w_p = v (p2 - p1), q_in = h3 - h2, w_t = h3 - h4 and efficiency = (w_t - w_p)/q_in from the steam tables.
Efficiency rises with higher boiler pressure or temperature and with lower condenser pressure.
The price is a wetter turbine exit, which limits the improvements.

questions.stem: In the ideal Rankine cycle, which process takes place in the condenser?

options.text: Isentropic compression of liquid
Isentropic expansion of wet steam
Constant-pressure heat rejection, ending as saturated liquid
Constant-pressure heat addition

questions.correctOptionText: Constant-pressure heat rejection, ending as saturated liquid
questions.explanation: The condenser removes heat from the turbine exhaust at constant pressure until it becomes saturated liquid. In the ideal cycle the pressure does not drop through the condenser.

questions.stem: Why is the pump work in a Rankine cycle very small compared with the turbine work?

options.text: Pumps are more efficient than turbines
The pressure rise is small
A liquid has a very small specific volume, so v (p2 - p1) is small
The pump is driven by the turbine

questions.correctOptionText: A liquid has a very small specific volume, so v (p2 - p1) is small

distractorRationale.b: The pressure rise is the same as the drop in the turbine.
distractorRationale.d: This does not change the amount.

questions.explanation: Work for an incompressible fluid is v times the pressure rise. Liquid water has a specific volume of about 0.001 m^3/kg, roughly a thousand times smaller than steam, so the work is tiny.

questions.stem: The condenser pressure of a Rankine cycle is lowered with the boiler state unchanged. What happens?

options.text: Efficiency falls and the turbine exit becomes drier
Efficiency rises and the turbine exit becomes drier
Efficiency is unchanged but the pump work rises
Efficiency rises and the turbine exit becomes wetter

questions.correctOptionText: Efficiency rises and the turbine exit becomes wetter

distractorRationale.b: The exit is wetter, not drier.
distractorRationale.c: Efficiency changes and pump work rises only slightly.

questions.explanation: A lower condenser pressure lowers the temperature at which heat is rejected and enlarges the turbine's enthalpy drop, so efficiency rises. The isentropic expansion then ends at a lower quality, so the exhaust steam is wetter.

questions.stem: On a T-s diagram of the ideal Rankine cycle, which line is vertical?

options.text: The boiler line 2-3
The turbine line 3-4 and the pump line 1-2
The condenser line 4-1
None of them

questions.correctOptionText: The turbine line 3-4 and the pump line 1-2

distractorRationale.a: The boiler is constant pressure, not constant entropy.
distractorRationale.d: Isentropic processes appear as vertical lines.

questions.explanation: Both the pump and the turbine are isentropic in the ideal cycle, so their lines are vertical on a T-s diagram. The boiler and condenser lines follow constant-pressure curves.

questions.stem: The boiler pressure of a Rankine cycle is raised while the peak temperature is held constant. Which pair of statements is correct?

options.text: The mean heat-addition temperature rises, so efficiency rises, and the exit becomes drier
The mean heat-addition temperature falls, so efficiency falls
The mean heat-addition temperature rises, so efficiency rises, but the turbine exit becomes wetter
The efficiency is unchanged because T3 is unchanged

questions.correctOptionText: The mean heat-addition temperature rises, so efficiency rises, but the turbine exit becomes wetter

distractorRationale.a: At a fixed peak T the exit becomes wetter.
distractorRationale.d: Mean temperature, not just peak, controls the efficiency.

questions.explanation: A higher boiling temperature raises the average temperature of heat addition, which raises efficiency, as for Carnot. With the peak temperature fixed, the isentropic expansion line starts farther left on the T-s diagram and reaches a lower quality at the condenser pressure.

questions.stem: Saturated liquid water (specific volume 0.001010 m$^3$/kg) is pumped from 10 kPa to 5 MPa in an ideal pump. Find the specific work in kJ/kg.
questions.explanation: For an incompressible liquid w = v (p2 - p1) = 0.001010 x (5000 - 10) = 5.04 kJ/kg, with pressures in kPa. This is small compared with the turbine work of roughly 1000 kJ/kg.

questions.stem: A Rankine plant circulates 40 kg/s of steam. The turbine specific work is 1020 kJ/kg and the pump specific work is 6 kJ/kg (values given). Find the net power output in MW.
questions.explanation: The net specific work is 1020 - 6 = 1014 kJ/kg. Multiplying by 40 kg/s gives 40560 kW = 40.56 MW.

questions.stem: A Rankine cycle has h1 = 192, h2 = 198, h3 = 3400 and h4 = 2250 kJ/kg (values given for the exercise). Find its thermal efficiency as a decimal fraction.
questions.explanation: Net work = (3400 - 2250) - (198 - 192) = 1144 kJ/kg and heat input = 3400 - 198 = 3202 kJ/kg. The efficiency is 1144/3202 = 0.3573.

questions.stem: Draw (describe) the ideal Rankine cycle on a T-s diagram and name the four processes with the device in which each takes place. Say what is constant in each.
markingGuide: 1-2 pump: isentropic compression of saturated liquid (vertical short line)
2-3 boiler: constant-pressure heat addition, passing through compressed liquid, boiling, and superheat
3-4 turbine: isentropic expansion (vertical line) to the condenser pressure
4-1 condenser: constant-pressure (and constant-temperature in the wet region) heat rejection to saturated liquid
State 1 on the saturated liquid line and state 3 in the superheated region (or on the saturated vapour line)
questions.explanation: Each device is identified with a process: the pump and turbine are isentropic, and the boiler and condenser are isobaric. The shape of the cycle on T-s shows how much of the heat addition is at high temperature.

questions.stem: Explain, using the idea of mean temperature of heat addition and rejection, why raising the boiler pressure and lowering the condenser pressure both raise the ideal Rankine efficiency. State the practical limitation that each change meets.
markingGuide: Efficiency rises when mean heat-addition temperature rises or heat-rejection temperature falls (Carnot analogy)
Higher boiler pressure raises the boiling temperature and mean addition temperature
Lower condenser pressure lowers the saturation temperature at which heat is rejected
Limitation: wetter turbine exit, blade erosion, lower exit quality
Condenser pressure limited by cooling water temperature and air in-leakage; boiler pressure limited by materials and cost
questions.explanation: Both changes widen the temperature gap across which the cycle operates, which raises the efficiency. The wetter exhaust steam, and the temperature of the available cooling water, impose the practical limits.
